parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a top-tier protective state (nondiscrimination since 2001, healthcare/public-accommodations coverage, hate-crime enhancements, shield listing) with a hostile federal layer that governs entry, passports, federal facilities and custody. Federal passport binary, visa-discrepancy refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal facility exclusion, and documented immigration-custody abuse are universal, state-imposed exposures not cancelled by state law. State protections materially reduce street/service risk, but do not offset federal screening, facilities or detention.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal X/mismatched markers stopped; Nov 2025 Supreme Court allowed restriction. Visa cable: document discrepancy/doubt on sex requires refusal and more evidence; suspected misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: State X on licences/birth certificates since 2020 and self-declaration change routes; existing X passports remain valid until expiry. No protection against federal entry rules documented.
entry_documents.interaction: State-issued documents do not govern federal passport/visa adjudication; an otherwise state-protected visitor still faces federal secondary inspection, refusal, or fraud consideration.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: transgender men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. Federal corrections from 2026 adopt hair-cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution model; trans prisoner numbers stopped being reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State hate-crime enhancements and nondiscrimination statutes documented; no operative federal custody placement protection or remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry/document discrepancy can lead to detention, where federal custody practices documented as harmful; state protections do not apply inside federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: January 2025 order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity federally. State itself has no mapped facility ban and allows gender-neutral single-occupancy toilets.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodations nondiscrimination since 2001; gender-neutral single-occupancy toilets from 2022 in state provisions.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State law protects in state/private venues, but federal buildings, airports and national facilities follow federal birth-sex rule; visitor must navigate both systems.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders and proposed rules restrict gender-affirming care for minors and public reimbursement under 18; national funding freeze and hospital subpoenas documented nationally.
care_services.protection: State added explicit patient-care/nursing nondiscrimination in June 2023 and is listed among shield-law/executive-order jurisdictions from 2023-2024 batches.
care_services.interaction: Shield measures may protect care obtained in-state, but scope for a visiting minor/adult and against federal action is unresolved in dossier; federal facilities/funding rules remain separate exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders define sex at birth, remove gender-identity workplace policies, direct investigation/prosecution over school social transition, and 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes radically pro-transgender groups. Several orders blocked/enjoined; passport restriction in effect.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment ruling (2020) and hate-crimes statute cover gender identity; state panic-defense repeal and enhancements. Litigation ongoing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat/hostility framing at federal level coexists with state protective statutes; enforcement by federal actors is not mitigated by state law.

minors_guardians.exposure: March 2025 school sports association shifted eligibility responsibility to schools under state/national law, replacing gender-identity participation rule. Federal orders target school transition support and minor care; 27 states ban minor care nationally per dossier context.
minors_guardians.protection: State conversion-therapy ban on minors since 2017, anti-bullying law, and shield-listing may protect minors in-state; scope for visiting families not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling trans minor faces state school-sport compliance shift plus federal care/policy hostility; guardian has no documented federal remedy.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific anti-trans violence incident or prevalence documented. Nationally, only 23 states cover gender identity in bias statutes; 2025 poll shows majority support birth-sex document laws.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime penalty enhancements for actual/perceived gender identity since statute 42-28-46, nondiscrimination in public accommodations, and documented Most Protective tier ranking.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State recourse exists on paper for street incidents, but federal policing/custody exposure is separate; absence of state violence data is not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; remedies depend on measures in effect at travel time. No enforcement data for state nondiscrimination provisions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit on passports, some federal orders enjoined, state complaint statutes exist; no documented visitor remedy against federal entry/facility decisions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation and state protections are partial and prospective; they do not currently restore X passports or federal facility access after Supreme Court allowed restriction.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: exclusion there is routine, universal and without effective remedy everywhere. Here state public-accommodations, healthcare and hate-crime protections operate for much of the visit, and imprisonment/execution are not documented outcomes, though federal entry exclusion is similarly remedy-poor.

Similar to or slightly below 0.55-B: both involve discretionary secondary screening, delay and possible refusal with slow appeals. This case adds a categorical federal facility ban, passport-marker prohibition allowed by Supreme Court, potential lifetime fraud finding, and documented custody abuse, pushing below 0.55.

Well below 0.75-C: there, matching passports are accepted, detention is brief, and counsel/compensation remedies work. Here federal law prohibits non-matching markers, instructs refusal on doubt, and several orders remain in effect or in litigation.

parsed.synthesis: The operative journey is bifurcated: state law, if applied, protects housing, services, healthcare and hate-crime recourse, but the visitor must first pass federal entry under binary passport rules, use federal facilities under birth-sex exclusion, and risk federal detention with documented abuse. That federal layer is a tier-1 universal exposure that state protections cannot cancel, while the absence of state violence/enforcement data leaves street risk uncertain. Net result is elevated risk, mitigated but not removed by state protections.
